description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) from the Whisper large model when various text preprocessing optimisations are applied, comparing performance between two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists five optimisation categories — “Normalised”, “Add Spacing”, “Remove Spacing”, “Americanisms”, and “Dates” — arranged from top to bottom. The horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large”, scaled from 0.0000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at 0.0000, 0.0010, 0.0020, and 0.0030. For each optimisation, two adjacent horizontal bars show the WER difference for each model, with exact values labeled at the end of each bar. The NESAC ft model consistently shows slightly higher WER differences than the SESHA ft model across all categories, with values ranging from 0.00257 (Dates) to 0.00334 (Normalised), while the SESHA ft model ranges from 0.00228 (Dates) to 0.00344 (Add Spacing). The chart visually suggests that while both models benefit from preprocessing, the SESHA ft model generally achieves lower WER differences — indicating better performance relative to Whisper large — particularly under “Dates” and “Americanisms”. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding for the two models.
